messages:
Jordan S.: FYI customer acme hit a burst of `dimension_mismatch` errors on /v1/embeddings after we rolled the dynbatch tweak. They also report intermittent tail latency spikes (~200-450ms). attaching short logs and a minimal repro.

Maya P.: Thanks — which model and client? did they change SDK version?

Jordan S.: Model: openembed-large-v1. Client: python-sdk v0.9.3. They send mixed small+large inputs in the same request stream. Example request body:

```json
{"model":"openembed-large-v1","input":["short text","a much longer piece of content ..."],"max_batch_size":64}
```

infra-bot: dynbatch.trace: flush_timer fired queue_size=3 max_batch_size=64 grace_ms=100 observed_input_shapes=[1536,1536,128] -> dispatched batch shapes mismatch -> routing to fallback.

Erin K.: Observed input shapes show a 128-dim vector in the queue. That explains the dimension_mismatch. Could be a downstream precomputed embedding slipping into the stream or client accidentally sending embedding instead of text.

Jordan S.: Customer confirms they sometimes forward precomputed vectors (128) mixed with raw text. They expected server to detect and route but got a hard error instead.

Jason H.: Two issues here: 1) mixed dims cause immediate failures; 2) dynbatch flushes small partial batches when a weird item appears, which can increase tail latency. Did we recently change default `max_batch_size` or `grace_ms` on that route?

ops-lee: We rolled max_batch_size 64 -> 32 for some customers last week to reduce memory OOMs, but not for acme. Their route still has 64. However we did lower `batching_grace_ms` globally to 50ms in the deploy. That increases flush frequency for small queues.

Maya P.: Repro plan: (A) Send mixed stream (text + 128-dim precomputed) to reproduce dim error; (B) Replay with different `batching_grace_ms` and `max_batch_size` to measure tail latency.

Jordan S.: Quick repro curl for (A):

```bash
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"openembed-large-v1","input":["hello world","[0.1,0.2,... (128 dims) ...]"]}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings
```

Erin K.: Immediate mitigation options for customer: 1) Validate client to block precomputed vectors (client-side fix); 2) Set `batching_grace_ms=200` and `max_batch_size=32` for the route to reduce flush churn; 3) Add server-side soft-check to reject inputs with numeric arrays unless `is_precomputed=true` header present.

embedsvc-bot: Incident created INC-2026-0783 assigned to eng-runtime (priority P2) — includes sample logs and traces from acme.

Jason H.: For long term: we should detect mixed-dim queues earlier in the batching pipeline and coalesce or split batches by detected dim. Also add a metric for "partial_batch_flush_rate" vs grace_ms so we can tune safely.

Jordan S.: Customer applied temporary client validation and reports errors stopped. They'll accept grace_ms=150 change while we roll a server fix. I'll document repro steps and customer evidence in the ticket.

Maya P.: Cool — can someone add a short playbook in support KB: avoid sending precomputed vectors to embeddings endpoint; how to set batching knobs; how to enable `X-Redwood-Debug: batch-trace` header for trace logs.

ops-lee: I'll put the KB draft in #docs-support and add a runbook to push route-level overrides.

Jordan S.: Thanks all. Follow-ups: eng-runtime to propose split-by-dim change; support to update KB; ops to offer temporary route config. :thumbsup:
